page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.3xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance allocates 12 dedicated virtual CPUs across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration provides 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache, alongside vector instruction support including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI.

Memory capacity is configured at an unconventional 1:1 vCPU-to-memory ratio, providing 12.0 GB of RAM in total, or 1.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmark evaluations reflect this compute-heavy profile: single-core metrics sit in lower percentiles with a Geekbench single-core score of 995.0 and weak single-threaded compression performance, whereas multi-core execution demonstrates stable mid-tier capability, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 5055.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 10093.16.

The instance does not bundle local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence, and includes a baseline network throughput of 4 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic workloads exhibit balanced throughput in web serving at 7.85 GB/sec and Redis operations at 8.63 million SET operations per second. However, memory-intensive operations score lower, evidenced by a PassMark memory score of 1653.05 and constrained execution on 7B parameter models.

From an efficiency standpoint, the instance trades memory capacity for concentrated multi-threaded CPU allocation. The limited 12 GB RAM footprint makes it unsuitable for large in-memory caching or big data analytics, but the balance of 12 vCPUs and AVX-512 support suits batch processing, multi-threaded compiling, web routing, and CPU-bound microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.3xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It provides 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores alongside 12.0 GB of system memory, establishing a tight 1 GB per core memory footprint. There is no bundled local storage and no hardware GPU accelerators, directing primary I/O through a 4 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate moderate multi-threaded performance, with a PassMark CPU score of 10093.16 and Geekbench multi-core score of 5055.0, paired with weaker single-core processing metrics. Instruction sets include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI for accelerated vector computing. Given its constrained memory-to-core ratio and solid multi-core execution, this instance is suited for multi-threaded batch operations, continuous integration build jobs, static web serving, and compute-focused microservice architectures.
